notes.subject: car
notes.text: Most coverage is low-quality, brownish "shitcam", often with a big round blur over the car; Nepal is entirely like this.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: All Generation 4 coverage is smallcam, mounted low with a large round blur and a small protrusion at the front.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: There are also many Generation 3 trekkers across the country.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Traffic drives on the left.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Many different scripts appear, and most can narrow down the region.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Fairly long plates; white is most common, commercial vehicles use yellow, and electric vehicles use green.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Black-and-white striped signposts are typical; Bangladesh, Nepal and Sri Lanka have them too.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: The most common pole is a square concrete pole with a trident-style top, though many regions have their own designs; wooden poles are very rare.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: The most widespread script has a line across the top of each word and many straight vertical strokes; it dominates the centre and north.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: A script like the northern one but with no line across the top of words.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: A softer-shaped script with a broken top bar and a curved mark under letters.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Script with many left-pointing triangular shapes, in the northeast; the same language is used next door in Bangladesh.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Smooth, round scripts with small circles are found in the south; Tamil has curves mixed with right angles and dot marks.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: A curvy script with wide semicircles over many letters, said to resemble a skull emoji.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Simple curvy letters, often with upside-down U shapes.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Signs are almost entirely in a Latin-script language here, unlike most of the country.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Yellow auto-rickshaws with black roofs are common in the south, mainly Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Concrete poles with see-through holes are unique to Gujarat and its neighbouring small territories.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Poles split into two sections, similar to Brazil, are common in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Metal poles with a mesh pattern are common in Sikkim.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Metal poles with holes are common in Kerala, along with small yellow pole markings.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Thin grey metal poles, often in pairs, appear across the northeast and the Himalayan states of Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Poles painted with five or more thin black and yellow stripes are found in the capital territory.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Exactly four thicker black and yellow stripes on poles mark Bihar, where trees may also have red-and-white stripes.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: A black stripe between two white ones on poles and trees is common in Tamil Nadu.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Southern roofs have neat, bright orange flat tiles with a ridge down the middle, especially in Tamil Nadu.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Round roof tiles in uneven rows are common in central areas.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Large hip roofs of corrugated metal are found in West Bengal and nearby parts of Bihar and Odisha.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: White-domed Sikh temples with ornate walls are most common in Punjab.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Thatched huts are mostly along the east coast and the northern plains; palm-fan thatch in the south, fine hay further north.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The tallest mountains are in the Himalayas; Ladakh and northern Himachal Pradesh are extremely dry and bare.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The northern plains are very fertile, flat and open farmland.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Western Rajasthan has dry, sandy ground.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Smooth conical pines with very long needles are almost exclusive to the northern Himalayan states.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Lush green valleys with low plants and eroded hills with many small peaks mark Mizoram; Meghalaya's hills are flatter-topped.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Islands packed with coconut palms, often painted red and white, mark Lakshadweep.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Planned city with blue sector signs, round yellow marks on lamp posts and street signs showing numbers rather than names.
